text:
For most reptile setups, I’d look for a **portable power station around 2,000 Wh** with an AC outlet, rather than a small phone-sized power bank. It could run a **24 W heat mat** for roughly **two days** under the estimate in this [runtime guide](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage); a **100 W ceramic heat emitter** cycling at about half power is closer to **one day**. Those are estimates, not measured runtimes, and actual results depend on the heater, thermostat, and station losses.

For a short outage or a low-wattage mat, a **300 Wh-class** station may cover around **6–8 hours**. Check that the station’s continuous output supports your heater, and plan to power the thermostat too if it needs electricity. If you share your heater’s wattage and how long you need backup, I can help size it more precisely.

While waiting for power, insulate the enclosure and keep the room closed; [Petco’s outage guidance](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage) also suggests emergency heat options such as wrapped warm-water bottles or hand warmers.
